title: Money Word Problems: Finding Cents Spent
intro: Use this worksheet to teach an unknown amount spent, rather than coin identification.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Represent the starting money with counters worth one cent each. Separate the amount left and identify the other part as the amount spent.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Before: 16 cents.

Spent: an unknown amount.

After: 7 cents remain.

16 − ? = 7
16 − 7 = 9

Alex spent 9 cents. The 9 cents spent and the 7 cents remaining account for all 16 cents.

Ask your student

How could we check that the money spent and the money left account for the starting amount?

If your student needs help

If the student answers with the amount left, have them complete the sentence about how much was spent.

Choosing and using the worksheet

These six questions focus on the unknown change in a spending situation. All quantities are below twenty. They are not a coin-identification activity or a worksheet about finding change from a cashier.
